chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

key_terms.عَدْل: Justice/Competence (in this context, equal standing in judgment)
key_terms.مَرْضِيّاً: Suitable/Approved (in terms of judgment and capability)

ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to arrange marriage for a grandson if both the father and grandfather are alive and disagree?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the hierarchy of guardianship (wilayah) in marriage, establishing that a suitable grandfather holds precedence over the father when both are of equal merit. The Imam’s preference for the grandfather’s choice in cases of equal standing reflects the Shia juristic view that the grandfather’s authority is more comprehensive, often rooted in the principle that he represents the broader lineage and family consensus. This ruling underscores the importance of familial harmony and the grandfather's role as a secondary but potent guardian in Shia family law.
